title: work
aim: Talk about first days, changing careers, video-call problems and teamwork.
objectives: Narrate past events with past perfect tenses
Explain tech problems and suggest solutions
Write a career report and a thank-you message

lessons.title: First day!
goals: Use past perfect simple and continuous
Tell a story with feelings and reactions

grammar.title: Past perfect simple and continuous
grammar.shortAr: الماضي التام لحدث انتهى قبل حدث آخر، والماضي التام المستمر لحدث استمر حتى نقطة في الماضي.
points: Past perfect simple: had + past participle for a completed action before another past action.
Past perfect continuous: had been + -ing for an activity in progress up to a past point.
Past simple carries the main events; past perfect forms give earlier background.
State verbs such as know, like and own normally use the past perfect simple.
table: had + past participle: earlier completed action
I'd only passed my test the year before.
had been + -ing: activity before a past point
I'd been trying to get a place for ages.
My foot slipped and I drove into the car behind me.
state verb: had known / had loved
exceptions: State verbs take the past perfect simple: I'd known him for years.
Past perfect continuous often explains a result visible later: She was tired because she'd been studying.

vocab.example: I hadn't driven for a while, so I felt nervous.
In no time, I'd met about twenty colleagues.
I destroyed his car just moments earlier.
I'd been trying to get a place for ages.
Up to that point I'd never been in a director's office.
By the time I noticed him, I'd already met thirty people.
At a reception you have to work the room.
I'd been making small talk for hours.
He laughed it off and said it didn't matter.

reading.summary: Three new employees recount embarrassing first-day incidents: a company-car crash, being trapped on the 22nd floor, and mistaking the company founder for an ordinary guest. Colleagues respond with humour and support.

listening.summary: Audio version of the first-day-at-work stories.
Connected-speech practice with had been in past perfect continuous sentences.

video.summary: Speakers say which professions they admire and why.

speaking: Tell a story about the first time you did something; include people's feelings and reactions.
writing: Write a short account of a first-day mistake, adding how you and others reacted.

practice.q: When I arrived, the meeting ___ for ten minutes.
practice.why: An earlier completed action before a past event takes the past perfect simple.

practice.q: She was exhausted because she ___ all morning.
practice.why: A continuous activity up to a past point uses had been + -ing.

practice.q: I ___ him before, so I knew who he was.
practice.why: Know is a state verb and normally uses the past perfect simple.

practice.q: By the time I got to the lift, I ___ my key card.
practice.why: The card was not provided before that moment, so the passive past perfect simple is needed.

lessons.title: Change of plan
goals: Discuss portfolio careers and career changes
Use structures for past plans and intentions

grammar.title: Past plans and intentions
grammar.shortAr: خطط سابقة تغيرت: was/were supposed/meant/going to/planning to + فعل، وthinking of/considering/planning on + -ing.
points: Was/were supposed to, meant to, going to, planning to, hoping to and expecting to take an infinitive.
Was/were thinking of, considering and planning on take the -ing form.
These forms describe intentions that changed or did not happen, unlike plans that were kept.
table: I was supposed to become a lawyer.
I wasn't meant to become a teacher.
She was planning to meet us, but her car broke down.
He was thinking of being a musician.
We were planning on staying in a hotel.
exceptions: Planning to meet and planning on meeting mean the same but take different forms.
For a plan that actually happened, use the past simple or past perfect instead.

vocab.example: A portfolio career can include several jobs you enjoy.
He wanted to advance his career.
She's a serial entrepreneur with three businesses.
He had a part-time job while at university.

vocab.ar: يغير مساره أو يعيد تعريف نفسه
vocab.example: Is there an age limit to reinventing yourself?

vocab.ar: يتدرب من جديد على مهنة أخرى
vocab.example: He retrained as an accountant.
She set up her own business.
He started out as an investment banker.
Is it best to switch careers in mid-life?

reading.summary: A BBC radio programme asks whether one career is enough and introduces portfolio careers, with guests offering different views on multiple jobs and new skills. Listeners' comments describe ambitions that changed.

listening.summary: Radio programme about the advantages and drawbacks of portfolio careers.
Check of work and career vocabulary from the programme.
Vocabulary bank practice on areas of work.
Pronunciation of the intrusive /w/ sound in past-intention phrases.

speaking: Tell a partner about a plan you had to change and how things turned out.
writing: Write a short report with an introduction, main issues and recommendations about young people's career choices.

practice.q: I ___ become a lawyer, but I changed my mind.
practice.why: A past intention with an infinitive that did not happen uses was supposed to.
Consider is followed by the -ing form.

practice.q: He ___ to become a doctor, but his grades weren't good enough.
practice.why: Planning to takes an infinitive; planning on takes -ing.

practice.q: We ___ in a hotel, but we found a cottage instead.
practice.why: Planning on is followed by -ing and signals a changed plan.

lessons.title: You're on mute!
goals: Suggest solutions and explain why they may work
Use intonation to sound more or less confident

grammar.title: Describing problems and suggesting solutions
grammar.shortAr: وصف عطل أو صعوبة، ثم اقتراح حل بلطف وتفسير سبب احتمال نجاحه.
points: Use I can't get the ... working / to work for a machine you cannot start.
Use keep + -ing for problems that happen repeatedly.
Suggest with Maybe/Perhaps you could + infinitive, Why don't you try + -ing, or It might be worth + -ing.
Explain a possible fix with That might work because ... or It sometimes helps if + infinitive.
table: I can't get the screen share working.
Perhaps you could try logging off and on again.
It might be worth checking the chat box.
It sometimes helps if you turn down the volume.
exceptions: Why don't you try is followed by -ing, but Maybe you could is followed by the infinitive without to.
It sometimes helps if takes an infinitive without to, not an -ing form.

vocab.example: Please stay on mute if you aren't speaking.
Remember to unmute yourself before you talk.
Check the webcam is at eye level.
The host checks the chat box regularly.
Respond to the invite before the meeting.
Check that no one is frozen on screen.
Post the document as a link in the chat box.
The host controls the meeting.
Make sure there isn't an echo or a delay.

reading.summary: The article lists practical rules for video meetings: reply to the invite, check the connection, light and background, keep the camera on, mute when silent, watch the chat box and check the sound.

listening.summary: Three video calls in which speakers break basic meeting rules.
Extracts with problem phrases and possible technical fixes.
Suggestions spoken with different intonation to show confidence.
More practice identifying confident suggestion intonation.
Model mediation exchange about expanding ideas and agreeing a solution.

speaking: Role-play a video call: explain a frozen screen or microphone problem, offer fixes and say when one works.
writing: Write a short chat message describing a call problem and two possible solutions.

practice.why: The fixed phrase is can't get the ... working.

practice.q: The picture ___ disappearing every few seconds.
practice.why: Keep + -ing describes a repeatedly occurring problem.
This suggestion pattern is followed by try + -ing.

practice.q: It sometimes helps ___ away from the mic.
practice.why: The pattern is it sometimes helps if + present simple.

lessons.title: Are you a team player?
goals: Compare working alone and in a team
Use non-defining relative clauses to comment

grammar.title: Non-defining relative clauses for comments
grammar.shortAr: جملة الموصول غير التحديدية تضيف تعليقاً أو رأياً بعد فاصلة، ولا تُستخدم لتحديد الشيء.
points: Defining clauses identify a person or thing; non-defining clauses add extra information.
Use which for things or whole clauses, who for people, whose for possession, where for places and when for times.
Non-defining clauses are set off with commas.
At the end of a sentence, they can comment on the whole previous statement.
table: We worked in a small office, which wasn't very comfortable.
My new boss, who is great to work with, started last week.
Nicky Laird, whose books I love, joined the team.
The summer, when the weather is better, is ideal.
I worked with Tim, which was a real pleasure.
exceptions: Do not use that in non-defining relative clauses.
For a comment on a whole clause, use which rather than what.

vocab.example: In a team you can share accomplishments.
Team members can support each other.
I'm self-employed, so working alone suits me.
I'm a bit of a perfectionist about my work.
In a team you can bounce ideas off other people.
We had to do the whole project online.
We had a group lunch, which was really fun.
I was in a dangerous situation, which was very scary.

reading.summary: Video interviews ask whether people prefer working alone or in a team; speakers mention shared achievements, mutual support, self-employment and a safety issue. Short extracts show how relative clauses add comments.

listening.summary: Review audio for a text about people who changed careers, including Obama, Armani and Harrison Ford.

video.summary: Street interviews about working alone or in a team and experiences of teamwork.

speaking: Discuss a successful team or solo experience and whether teams usually achieve better results.
writing: Write a thank-you message to teammates, explaining what they did and why it mattered.

practice.q: My old team left everything to the last minute, ___ was frustrating.
practice.why: Which refers back to the whole previous clause.

practice.q: We had a group lunch, ___ was really fun.
practice.why: A comment on an event uses which.

practice.q: Yuki, ___ joined last year, has had a positive impact.
practice.why: Who refers to a person in a non-defining clause.

practice.q: The building, ___ was built in 1882, is being redecorated.
practice.why: Non-defining clauses take which, not that.

review.summary: Review of first-day stories, changed career plans, call troubleshooting and comments on teamwork, with a career-change reading text.
tasks: Rewrite sentences using past perfect simple or continuous.
Complete past-intention sentences with the correct infinitive or -ing form.
Finish the career-change article and check answers with the review audio.

quiz.q: When I got to the restaurant, I realised I ___ my purse at home.
I was tired because I ___ for two hours.
I ___ physics at university, but I didn't get the grades.
The colleague ___ car I had destroyed was very understanding.
Which expression means 'for a very long time'?
A career made up of several different jobs is a ___ career.
If you aren't speaking on a video call, stay ___.

options: She got trapped on the 22nd floor.
She mistook the CEO for an ordinary guest.
She forgot her key card at home.
quiz.answer: She mistook the CEO for an ordinary guest.

quiz.q: What is the main point of the career report on young people?
options: Traditional jobs are the only secure jobs.
Young people's ambitions lag behind changing work.
quiz.answer: Young people's ambitions lag behind changing work.

quiz.q: A webcam image has stopped moving. Best problem phrase:
options: There seems to be a problem with my picture.
It might be worth a picture.
I can't get the chat box.
That might work because the picture.
quiz.answer: There seems to be a problem with my picture.

quiz.q: Polite suggestion for a tech problem:
options: Maybe you could try logging off and on again.
Log off and don't ask again.
quiz.answer: Maybe you could try logging off and on again.

quiz.q: Which sentence adds a comment about the previous statement?
options: The team that I work with won awards.
We worked in a small office, which was uncomfortable.
The office which is small is new.
The man who called is here.
quiz.answer: We worked in a small office, which was uncomfortable.
